title: Major depression: episode, severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's depressive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for depression.

HPI
The patient is an 86-year-old male presenting for a follow-up evaluation of his mood. He reports that his symptoms have significantly worsened over the last month. He describes a pervasive sense of sadness, profound fatigue, and a loss of interest in activities he previously enjoyed, such as gardening and spending time with his grandchildren. He reports significant sleep disturbances, specifically early morning awakening, and a noticeable decrease in appetite. He states that he feels "heavy" and "hopeless" most of the day. He denies any thoughts of self-harm. He notes that he is struggling to complete basic daily tasks and feels a lack of energy to engage with his peers. He denies any perceptual disturbances or a break from reality.

Review of Systems
Negative for chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. Negative for tremors or tremors. Negative for weight changes. Negative for fever or chills. Negative for visual or auditory changes. Negative for any changes in thought content.

Social History
The patient is retired and lives with his wife in a single-story home. He enjoys walking in his garden and watching news programs. He does not smoke and drinks only occasional glasses of wine with dinner.

Family History
Father had hypertension and a history of depression. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Vitals
Temperature: 98.4 F
Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air
Weight: 178 lbs

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 14.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.5 x 10^3/uL
Glucose: 108 mg/dL
eGFR: 68 mL/min/1.73m2

Medication List
Sertraline 50mg daily
Lisinopril 10mg daily

Exam
The patient appears well-groomed but shows a slumped posture and a flat affect. He is cooperative but speaks with a low volume and slow rate. He is oriented to person, place, and time. Cognition is intact for his age. Mood is described as "very low." Speech is normal in content but diminished in volume. No evidence of tremors or gait instability.

Assessment
The patient's symptoms are consistent with a major depressive disorder, single episode. The current episode is characterized as severe without psychotic features. He is not currently showing evidence of any perceptual disturbances.

Plan
Continue current dose of Sertraline. We will monitor his response to the current regimen. The patient was advised to contact the office immediately if his symptoms worsen or if he experiences an increase in hopelessness. Follow-up in four weeks.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features (HCC 155): F32.2.
